stimulus.inline: **A learner is asked to apply the repayment BEFORE the interest in a loan model. Why is this wrong?**

items.question: Explain in your own words why interest is added FIRST, then repayment subtracted.
items.expectedAnswer: The bank charges interest based on what you OWED during the month. If you subtract your repayment first, you'd be paying interest only on the smaller post-repayment balance, but you actually had the full opening balance outstanding for most of the month. So interest must be added to the opening balance (the amount actually owed) BEFORE deducting the repayment, otherwise the bank is essentially crediting your repayment as having been there all along, which it wasn't.
workingSteps: Identify which balance the interest is actually charged on (the opening balance).
Explain why pre-applying the repayment understates the interest.
Frame in terms of cash flow timing.

stimulus.inline:
**Sandile is comparing two loan models, both R20 000 over 12 months:**
- Loan A: 1,5%/month compound, repays R1 850/month.
- Loan B: 2%/month compound, repays R1 900/month.

items.question: Which loan has a higher closing balance after row 1 (and is therefore taking longer to pay off)?
workingSteps: Higher closing = Loan B. (NB tutor: answer says A higher — verify. B is higher by R50.) Re-check: A = 18 450, B = 18 500. B has higher closing → Loan B is paid down more slowly in month 1. Note answer key has Loan A wrong; correct is Loan B.

stimulus.inline: **Mpho deposits R10 000 in a fixed deposit at 8% per annum compound (no further deposits or withdrawals). 5-year table.**

items.question: Calculate the total interest earned over the 5 years.

stimulus.inline: **A teacher's retirement annuity model: R500/month contribution, 7% per annum compound (≈0,583%/month) over 30 years.**

items.question: Roughly, will the final balance be more or less than R500 000? Explain your reasoning without doing the full calculation.
items.expectedAnswer: It will be substantially MORE than R500 000. Over 30 years (360 months), the contributions alone total 360 × R500 = R180 000. With 7% per annum compound growth on a steadily-growing balance, the interest earned over three decades would more than double or triple the contributed amount. A rough estimate would put the final balance around R600 000 to R800 000.
workingSteps: Note that compound growth over 30 years multiplies invested capital several times.
Estimate: contributions alone are R180k, with compounding the total will be much higher.

stimulus.inline: **A short loan: R5 000, 2%/month compound, R600/month repayment.**

items.question: How many months does it take to pay off the loan?
workingSteps: Build the model: each month opening grows by 2%, then R600 is subtracted.
Continue until balance ≤ 600 (final month repayment may be smaller).
Result: approximately 9 months to pay off.

stimulus.inline: **Lebo invests R1 000 once and adds R100/month at 0,5%/month compound for 12 months.**

items.question: What is the balance after 12 months?
workingSteps: Start at R1 000. Each month: interest = balance × 0,005, then add R100.
After 12 months of building this table (or using future value of annuity formulas), balance ≈ R2 300. Acceptable range R2 270 to R2 330.

_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_REPAYMENT_BEFORE_INTEREST: Subtracts the repayment from the opening balance BEFORE adding the interest (gives too little interest)
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_BALANCE_GROWTH_BASE: Calculates interest on the wrong balance (e.g. uses original principal each month instead of current opening balance)
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_COMPOUND_AS_SIMPLE: Models the scenario with simple interest when compound is required
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_TOTAL_VS_INTEREST: Reports closing balance when asked for interest, or vice versa
